## Correction to the comment above: two distinct failure modes, not three of one

The previous comment said the timeout "is the observed mode in all three reproductions". That is
wrong about the original. Re-reading this ticket's own description, the 2026-10-26 failure was the
**assertion** mode:

> The failing assertion is the detector's:
> `assert any("maintenance" in o for o in offenders)`
> so `commits >= 1` held — commits WERE traced — but with `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` emptied, git ran no
> maintenance/gc/repack/pack-objects/multi-pack-index process as a descendant of a `git commit`.

So the record is 3 failures across **2 distinct modes**:

| Date | Story / worktree | Mode | Reaches `_maintenance_diagnosis`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-26 | `b6e723ceb59` | assertion — `offenders` empty, commits traced | yes |
| 2026-10-31 | `8257` / `impl-8257` @ `9424881459c` | `RebarError`: git timed out after 30s | no |
| 2026-11-01 | `c670` / `impl-c670` @ `938e962c5d8` | `RebarError`: git timed out after 30s | no |

That changes what the open decision buys rather than invalidating it. Gerrit 3135's diagnosis is
correctly aimed at the mode that produced this ticket, and it would still fire if that mode recurs.
What the two newer failures show is that the **more frequent** mode on this host — 2 of 3, both
within the last 48 hours — raises inside `_create_two_tickets_traced` at
`test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py:186` and so collects no evidence at all.

The three candidate mechanisms in the description remain neither ruled in nor out: none of them is
tested by a timeout, because the timeout aborts before git's maintenance decision can be observed.
Reproduction attempts for the **assertion** mode stay at 4 attempts, 0 reproductions.

Whether the two modes share a root cause is unestablished. They are consistent with one — a commit
that runs long enough under load either exceeds the 30s bound or gets its maintenance work cut
short, which is candidate mechanism 2 — but nothing here measures that, and the timeout path
captures neither the commit duration nor the trace that would distinguish it.
